Turn an intention into a proposed action.

A person defines the task and relevant design context. An assistant may propose a sequence of changes or tool calls. The September 2026 material describes partial assistance through command-line and Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflows.

A command-line interface exposes an explicit operation. MCP provides a way for an assistant to call exposed tools. Neither interface establishes that a proposed operation is physically appropriate or safe to accept without review.

Application and review remain human responsibilities.

The described workflow includes human application and review of proposals. Before accepting a change, inspect its target, parameters and effect on the design. After tool execution, compare the output with the intended engineering question.

An apparently successful tool call can still use the wrong geometry, boundary condition or interpretation. A failed or incomplete call needs an explicit outcome before further actions build on it. This is not evidence of autonomous end-to-end chip design.

Design and Simulation
↗
Know where the information goes.

The local solver and the assistant are separate processing boundaries. Running a solver locally does not establish that every prompt, design excerpt or returned result remains local. The supplied summary does not settle which assistant providers or external processing settings apply to a particular deployment.

Before sharing sensitive work, confirm which data leaves the machine, which service receives it, retention settings and access permissions. No blanket confidentiality guarantee is made here; the initial enquiry should describe a non-confidential task.

Inspect the whole sequence, including failures.

A useful demonstration should show the user instruction, proposed action, accepted changes, executed command and inspected result. It should also show what happens when a tool is unavailable or the output is ambiguous.

The current source supports partial workflow assistance. Broader automation, unattended reliability and current access remain questions for a scoped demonstration.
